rationale: Select the first-ranked feasible method, data-parallel over inputs. The sealed whole-workload concurrent-throughput bound on one GPU is 1.769286772300605x (p=1; k=min(8, measured concurrency factor 1.769286772300605); MPS enabled), not an additional kernel-only multiplier or a guaranteed implementation speedup. Kernels account for 60.41077234248375% of wall time and CUDA API host time for 39.174055662981827%; concurrent independent work can exploit the measured throughput opportunity across the workload. H2D and D2H together account for only 0.4151719945344284%, consistent with the supplied pipelining bound of just 1.0020801781311908x. GPU utilization is unavailable, so no utilization claim is inferred. The packet contains one scientific input; concurrency must therefore dispatch existing independent input/replica-seed work items without inventing new scientific inputs or changing the ensemble. Scheduling, process/context startup, CPU contention, device contention, synchronization, and result collection can reduce realized gains.
plan_steps: In a later implementation phase, identify the existing workload entry point and dispatch boundary. Represent each already scheduled independent task by input identity, replica seed, and seed block; retain exactly the existing workload, scientific parameters, outputs, and sealed method label data-parallel over inputs.

Add a bounded worker dispatcher using the single GPU with the supplied MPS configuration. Give each worker isolated simulation state and output storage. Start evaluation with two concurrent existing tasks; treat eight as the supplied fixed concurrency cap, not as measured optimal worker count or promised speedup. Do not split a trajectory or introduce coupling between replicas.

Preserve the existing model, precision, integration settings, step count, initialization, and output calculations. Use identical replica seeds for both Langevin integration and initial velocities in baseline and method arms. Collect results by stable task identity, independent of completion order, and preserve existing aggregation semantics.

Use the unchanged sealed timing schedule: 12 timing pairs per method/budget, on one GPU at equal cost. Include dispatch, initialization, synchronization, collection, and tail overhead in whole-workload timing. Report throughput against the supplied 1.769286772300605x bound without multiplying it by a separate stage speedup.

Run the unchanged scientific comparison for the one input and seeds 2000 through 2015, paired by input identity, replica seed, and seed block. Use the first scheduled completed baseline/method pair at each method/budget for scientific differences; timing repeats are not independent seeds. Missing seeds, nonfinite outputs, changed step counts, and failed trajectories invalidate the comparison.

For each energy metric, compute method-minus-baseline differences per seed and exact two-sided order-statistic 95% confidence bounds for the median paired difference. Require the entire interval strictly inside [-38.645762407664954, 38.645762407664954] kJ/mol for mean_potential_kj_mol and [-103.4640734063755, 103.4640734063755] kJ/mol for final_potential_kj_mol. Keep seeds, margins, confidence rule, budgets, and method fixed; do not extend seeds or widen margins after results. Accept implementation only if the sealed scientific and timing checks pass.

risks: Only one input is supplied. Feasibility depends on exposing already independent replica-seed work items through the input-task dispatcher; concurrency must not add replicas, alter seeds, or relabel the method as ensembles or batching.

GPU resource guards have passed, but startup overhead, host API contention, GPU contention, task imbalance, and synchronization can lower throughput below the sealed bound. The fractional measured factor is not a worker count.

Concurrent CUDA execution can alter floating-point behavior and stochastic trajectories despite identical seeds. Shared random state, mutable simulation state, output collisions, completion-order aggregation, or mismatched seed blocks could also compromise equivalence and require prevention.

Frozen energy margins derive from cross-seed Monte Carlo standard errors over seeds 1000 through 1007. They are neither same-seed repeatability estimates nor published scientific tolerances, and passing these metrics does not establish equivalence for untested observables.

The stated power is conditional on independent, centered normal paired differences with standard deviation at most one quarter of each margin. Actual paired variance is unavailable; the stated approximately 0.99899 per comparison and at least 0.9817 joint power across 18 comparisons are not measured or unconditional guarantees. Preserve the fixed 16-seed protocol even if observed variance is larger.
